import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a clean style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a single figure for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Define a specific order for BMI categories for consistent plotting and legend
bmi_order = ['Normal', 'Overweight', 'Obese']
df['BMI Category'] = pd.Categorical(df['BMI Category'], categories=bmi_order, ordered=True)

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration, Quality of Sleep,
# BMI Category (hue), and Stress Level (size).
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df.sort_values('BMI Category'), # Sort to ensure consistent legend order
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='BMI Category',
    size='Stress Level',
    sizes=(100, 500), # Adjust marker sizes for better visibility and distinction
    palette='viridis', # Choose a color palette for BMI categories
    alpha=0.8, # Set transparency for points
    legend='full' # Show the full legend for hue and size
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality by BMI Category and Stress Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Improve readability with grid and tick formatting
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Adjust legend position to prevent overlap with data points
plt.legend(title='BMI Category & Stress Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/titles from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png')
